title: Dense commensurators of infinite normal lattice subgroups also commensurate the ambient irreducible lattice in characteristic zero
source_title: Commensurators of normal subgroups of lattices
author: David Fisher; Mahan Mj; Wouter van Limbeek
difficulty_reason: The usual finite-index-subgroup counting argument fails when the infinite normal subgroup is not finitely generated. The authors use the locally finite Cayley-Abels graph to construct a finite-index subgroup as a finite-ball stabilizer and prove that its fibers are invariant under the whole lattice. This new normalization construction then lets discrete normalizers force the two ambient lattices to be commensurable, beyond the classical rigidity and normalizer prerequisites alone.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Proposition2.8 in the standing Theorem1.3 setting: finite product of almost simple algebraic groups over characteristic-zero local fields, irreducible latticeLambda, infinite normal subgroupGamma and dense commensuratorDelta. Delta commensuratesLambda; consequentlyLambda is arithmetic in the appropriateT-arithmetic formulation. Read all new finite-ball/fiber stabilizer construction11–12 and Schlichting/Cayley-Abels context7–8/11. Margulis normal subgroup theorem reduces higher rank, Margulis commensurator rigidity supplies arithmeticity, and discreteness of the normalizer of a discrete Zariski-dense subgroup is the explicitly used prior Lie-group foundation. No finite-generation assumption onGamma; finite generation of the characteristic-zero lattice is essential to the graph construction. No characteristic-positive/reducible conclusion asserted. The later central-extension proof and supergroup lemma were previewed but their stronger full theorem is not separately counted. historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors pass to a Cayley-Abels graph of a relative profinite completion to build a finite-index subgroup of a possibly infinitely generated normal subgroup that is normalized by the lattice. Discrete normalizers then force the lattice and its commensurator conjugates to be commensurable, beyond qualifying-exam lattice theory.
